blocks.text: The chapter presents Judah’s response to invasion as a movement from fear and acknowledged helplessness to prayer, prophetic instruction, praise, and deliverance. Jehoshaphat does not claim that Judah can defeat the coalition; he gathers the people at the temple and confesses, “we do not know what to do,” while fixing their attention on the LORD. Jahaziel’s message then frames the coming encounter as God’s battle, and Judah goes out praising before it sees the outcome. This sequence fits a recurring pattern in Judah’s story in which seeking the LORD, humbling oneself, praying, and receiving prophetic instruction stand in contrast to abandoning the LORD.
